pairs.why: B's blue zip with a chunky slider tab reads as a real, fully built bag, like the preferred lesson objects with clear readable parts; A's plain blue strip is simpler and less convincing.
A has the slider tab, which makes it read as a real zip bag; B's bare blue strip looks generic, and the two are otherwise the same in finish and light.
A's chunky slider zip at the edge matches the bold, simple toy-like build of the real cards; B's thin film above the zip and its flatter top are more fussy and photographic.
B's bold slider zip reads cleaner and more game-like, while A's wrinkled film flap above the zip looks more photographic and less like the real cards.
Both have the same slider-zip design, smooth plastic and lighting; they differ only in framing, which doesn't separate them.
Both are near-identical slider-zip bags with the same rendering and finish; neither is meaningfully closer to the real cards.
B's chunky slider zip gives a bold, readable build like the real cards; A's film flap and thinner zip look more photographic.
